args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION

MEMORANDUM
RE: Counterparty Markup of CFIUS National Security Agreement — Risk-Prioritized Markup Analysis, Recommendations, and Counter-Draft Language

To: Deal Team
From: International Trade & Sanctions Practice
Date: [Current Date]
Re: Analysis of Counterparty Markup against Draft National Security Agreement

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have reviewed the counterparty's markup of the draft CFIUS National Security Agreement ("draft NSA") against the base deal materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the deal team correspondence. The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations that must be negotiated: (1) a silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket; (2) the addition of Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") carve-outs for regulatory action of precisely the kind at issue in this matter; and (3) a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B's survival matrix.

Consistent with the latest, controlling partner instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible-to-tipping). By contrast, the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue, and it must not be conceded. The indemnification cap reduction and the MAE carve-outs are also material and should be resisted on the basis of the disclosure schedules.

This memorandum sets out, in descending order of risk, each material change, the controlling rule from the supporting materials, our recommendation, and counter-draft language for each.

II. SOURCE RECONCILIATION AND CONTROLLING PRINCIPLES

The draft NSA contains representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions. Three sets of supporting materials qualify and govern the review:

1. Disclosure Schedules. The scheduled exceptions narrow the base representations and control over general statements:
   - Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs.
   - Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift from seller to buyer.
   - Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the markup's limitation-period change contradicts.

2. Deal Team Correspondence. The latest partner message controls and supersedes all earlier messaging. Under the controlling instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.

3. Misfiled Correspondence. The matter folder contains administrative correspondence from an unrelated engagement (administrative file 20). It was misfiled and MUST NOT be relied upon for this analysis. It has been disregarded.

III. RISK-PRIORITIZED ISSUES

ISSUE 1 (WALK-AWAY / HIGHEST RISK): SHORTENED SURVIVAL PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
Counterparty Change: The markup adds a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations.
- Base materials: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix; the markup's limitation-period change contradicts Exhibit B.
- Controlling instruction: The client treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This is not negotiable.
- Recommendation: REJECT in its entirety. Restore survival to Exhibit B. Do not concede any reduction.
- Counter-Draft Language:
  "Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the survival period for each representation and warranty set forth in Exhibit B shall remain as set forth in Exhibit B, and no amendment or markup shall reduce, shorten, or otherwise modify the survival of, or the time to assert a claim for breach of, any representation or warranty set forth therein. Any purported reduction of such survival periods shall be void."

ISSUE 2 (HIGH RISK): SILENT REDUCTION OF THE INDEMNIFICATION CAP AND SHIFTING OF RETAINED LIABILITIES
Counterparty Change: The indemnification cap is silently reduced, and the basket is converted from a deductible to a tipping basket.
- Base materials: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift from seller to buyer.
- Contractual effect: A reduced cap concentrates exposure into a smaller recovery band; the deductible-to-tipping conversion changes the economics of when indemnification begins to pay. Per Schedule 5.2, these changes would shift retained liabilities that the parties previously agreed seller would bear.
- Controlling instruction: The client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible-to-tipping). The cap reduction is a separate and independent change and is not conceded.
- Recommendation: CONCEDE the basket conversion per the controlling partner instruction. REJECT the silent cap reduction; reinstate the negotiated cap and expressly preserve Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation.
- Counter-Draft Language (cap):
  "The aggregate liability of the Seller pursuant to this Agreement shall not exceed the indemnification cap set forth in the base draft of this Agreement as of the date of execution, which cap shall not be reduced or otherwise modified. All retained liabilities set forth in Schedule 5.2 shall remain the sole responsibility of the Seller, and no provision of this Agreement shall be construed to shift, transfer, or allocate any such retained liability to the Buyer."
- Counter-Draft Language (basket, conceded):
  "[Conceded — confirm as negotiated:] The basket set forth in this Agreement shall operate as a tipping basket in accordance with the counterparty markup, such that once the aggregate amount of Losses exceeds the basket threshold, Seller shall be responsible for all such Losses."

ISSUE 3 (HIGH RISK): ADDITION OF MAE CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
Counterparty Change: The definition of "Material Adverse Effect" adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.
- Base materials: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. These are live, material inquiries specific to the target.
- Contractual effect: A general carve-out for "regulatory action" would exclude from the MAE definition precisely the regulatory exposure that is pending and material to this transaction, effectively nullifying the MAE representation and any related closing condition.
- Recommendation: REJECT the carve-outs to the extent they would carve out the pending inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7. Amend so that any regulatory-action carve-out expressly excludes the two disclosed inquiries.
- Counter-Draft Language:
  "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the definition of 'Material Adverse Effect,' no exception or carve-out for any regulatory action, investigation, enforcement proceeding, inquiry, or similar matter shall apply to, or exclude from the definition of Material Adverse Effect, (i) the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7, (ii) any facts, circumstances, or conditions underlying such inquiries, or (iii) any Loss arising from or relating thereto. Any such carve-out shall be without effect as to the foregoing."

IV. RECOMMENDATION SUMMARY

[Table]
| Issue | Risk Level | Recommendation | Counter-Draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Survival-period reduction | Walk-away | Reject in full; restore Exhibit B | Provided |
| Indemnification cap reduction | High | Reject; reinstate cap; preserve Schedule 5.2 | Provided |
| MAE regulatory-action carve-outs | High | Reject as to Schedule 3.7 inquiries | Provided |
| Basket conversion (deductible→tipping) | Conceded | Accept per controlling instruction | Provided |

V. CONCLUSION

The counterparty markup is largely consistent with firm-standard practice, but it contains three material deviations requiring negotiation. The survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue under the controlling partner instruction and must be rejected. The indemnification cap reduction and the MAE carve-outs, which intersect the disclosed regulatory inquiries and the retained-liability schedule, must also be rejected or conformed as set forth above. The basket conversion may be conceded consistent with the client's stated position. The misfiled administrative correspondence from the unrelated engagement was disregarded entirely and does not affect this analysis.

Please advise if you would like us to prepare a full blackline of the draft NSA incorporating the counter-draft language above.

[signed] International Trade & Sanctions Practice
